terms.definition: A family in which partners share roles more equally, as Young and Willmott claimed was developing.
terms.examiner: Oakley's research is the classic challenge: men "helping" is not equal sharing.

terms.definition: Joint roles are shared tasks and leisure; segregated roles are separate male and female tasks.
terms.examiner: Bott's terms; useful for describing change over time.

terms.definition: Women doing paid work and still doing most of the housework and childcare.
terms.examiner: A feminist concept; add the triple shift (emotional work) for development.

terms.definition: Paid work, domestic work and emotional work, all carried by women.
terms.examiner: Duncombe and Marsden; links to the stabilisation-of-personalities debate.

terms.definition: The work of managing relationships and the feelings of family members.
terms.examiner: Often invisible in time-use studies; a good evaluation point.

terms.definition: Who has the final say on important family decisions such as money and moving house.
terms.examiner: Pahl and Vogler on control of money show inequality persisting in dual-earner couples.

terms.definition: Physical, sexual, psychological or financial abuse between partners or family members.
terms.examiner: Radical feminists see it as an outcome of patriarchy; contrast with explanations based on stress and poverty.

terms.definition: The replacement of household tasks by goods and services bought in the market.
terms.examiner: Used to argue domestic labour has fallen, though not necessarily become equal.

terms.definition: A man who takes an equal share of domestic work and childcare.
terms.examiner: Evidence suggests the idea outruns practice; use time-use data.

terms.definition: Shared expectations of the roles men and women should play.
terms.examiner: Same-sex couples, as in Dunne's research, show roles negotiated more equally when scripts are absent.
